Delafosse and Niane held Niani to be the capital for most of the empire's history; 'Several 21st century historians have firmly rejected Niani as a capital candidate', and 'no firm evidence of royal residence has come to light'. 'Kangaba became the last refuge of the Keita royal family after the collapse of the Mali Empire'. The point is the gazetteer's Niani; the page gives no coordinates.

The ledger puts them back.

Mansa Musa page: 'The Mali Empire comprised land that is now part of Guinea, Senegal, Mauritania, the Gambia' with 'an area of 1,300,000 km2' and 'incorporating the cities of Gao and Timbuktu into its territory'. Infobox figures: 1350 1,300,000 km2 and 1380 1,100,000 km2 against 973,312 km2 here (ratios 0.75 and 0.88): within the factor of two, the shape is on the small side.

ledger.note: Undated, within Sundiata's reign (c. 1235 to c. 1255): Diafunu and Kita are conquered. The Sundiata page lists the conquest of Diafunu and Kita. It names no ruler or people there; 1241 is Cliopatria's shape break, a bridge. The location is the researcher's reading (both lie in the Kayes region of western Mali).

ledger.counterpart: Senegambian chieftaincies (the page names the Bainuk king Kikikor)
ledger.note: Undated, within Sundiata's reign: Senegambia and Kaabu are conquered under his general Tiramakhan. The Sundiata page has Tiramakhan conquer Senegambia (present-day Senegal, the Gambia and Guinea-Bissau) and the Bainuk king Kikikor killed and the state renamed Kaabu. The Kaabu page does not mention Sundiata and puts the 'unification under Tiramakhan Traore' in the 13th century. Jolof (next event) and Takrur (1285) are taken out. 1241 is a bridge.

region.text: Jolof, the Wolof country of central Senegal

ledger.note: Undated, within Sundiata's reign: Jolof is made a Mali vassal. The Sundiata page has Jolof's king defeated by Tiramakhan and reduced to a vassal state. The Jolof Empire proper is founded only c. 1360 (Jolof page); the page's Jolof is the earlier Wolof kingdom. 1241 is a bridge.

Audaghost

ledger.counterpart: Oualata and Audaghost (holders not named on the page)
ledger.note: Undated, under Sundiata's generals: the northern marches Oualata and Audaghost are taken. 'Sundiata's generals continued to expand the empire's frontiers, reaching from Kaabu in the west' ... 'Takrur, Oualata and Audaghost in the north, and the Soninke Wangara goldfields in the south.' The page names no previous holder; Takrur is deferred to 1285 on the Takrur page's date. 1241 is a bridge.

c. 1285: Mali conquers Takrur. 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'; infobox 'Conquered and vassalized by Mali Empire: c. 1285'. The Mali page lists Takrur among the northern marches reached by Sundiata's generals, undated; the dated Takrur page is followed.

c. 1300: Mali takes Gao. 'Gao had become prosperous enough to attract the Mali Empire's attention' around 1300, and Mali 'took the city and collected taxes until the 1430s'. The Mali page says Gao 'was annexed into the Mali Empire by either Mansa Sakura or Mansa Musa'; Mansa Musa page: Saghmanja conquered Gao, undated. The page names the city, not a state; the counterpart is the Gao kingdom that became the Songhai Empire.

1324: Mansa Musa annexes Timbuktu peacefully on his way to Mecca. 'Timbuktu, which he peaceably annexed in 1324'; the Mansa Musa page: 'incorporating the cities of Gao and Timbuktu into its territory'.

c. 1360: Jolof becomes permanently independent of Mali. 'Jolof was a vassal of the Mali Empire for much of its early history'; 'the Jolof became permanently independent during a succession dispute c. 1360' (Ogot); Mali page 'During this period the Jolof Empire was founded, and soon dominated all of northern Senegambia'.
1433: the Tuareg take Timbuktu. 'In 1433-1434, the Empire lost control of Timbuktu to the Tuareg, led by Akil Ag-Amalwal.'

c. 1430s: Gao leaves Mali. Infobox 'Independence from Mali Empire: c. 1430s'; Mali had taken the city and 'collected taxes until the 1430s'. The Mali page puts the area around Gao independent of Malian control after the 1370s war with the Tuareg of Takedda, and the Songhai page says dynastic instability in the 1380s and 90s 'likely allowed the Songhai to formalize their independence'; the dossier follows the infobox.
c. 1436: the Tuareg take Oualata. 'Three years later, Oualata also fell into their hands', three years after 1433-1434.

region.text: Mema, west of Timbuktu, and the Niger lands lost with it

ledger.note: 1465: Songhai conquers Mema. 'The rising Songhai Empire conquered Mema, one of Mali's oldest possessions, in 1465.' (The Songhai page has Sonni Sulayman Dama attack Mema in the 1460s.) The land is read as the difference between Cliopatria's 1463 and 1468 shapes, since Mema is not in the gazetteer.

region.text: the northern Sahel lands between the 1474 and 1475 shapes

ledger.note: Page silent on Mali for 1475; the Cliopatria shape drops to 13.9 N. Songhai incorporated Djenne in 1473 after a seven-year siege and the Mossi raided Macina in 1477 (Mali page); the loss of the northern Niger lands is bridged to Songhai at 1475.

1502: Songhai takes Diafunu. 'Songhai forces under the command of Askia Muhammad I defeated the Mali general Fati Quali Keita in 1502 and seized the province of Diafunu.' The page gives no location; Nioro du Sahel is the researcher's proxy, and the province lies north of the 1475 shape (no change in the drawn shape).

region.text: Kaabu: Guinea-Bissau, the Gambia and the Senegalese Casamance

ledger.note: 1537: Kaabu breaks away. Infobox 'Independence from the Mali Empire: 1537'; 'It rose to prominence as an imperial military province of the Mali Empire'; Mali's western provinces 'were cut off by the expanding power of Koli Tenguella in the early 16th century'. The land is the Kaabu page's 'northeastern Guinea-Bissau, large parts of today's Gambia' and the Casamance.

ledger.note: By 1576: Mali reasserts authority over Wuli on the north bank of the Gambia. 'The breakup of the Wolof Empire allowed Mali to reassert authority over some of its former subjects' on the north bank of the Gambia, 'such as Wuli, by 1576.' The region is the whole Gambia, wider than Wuli.

notes: Cliopatria's nine Mali shapes are corrected in four places. (1) 1236-1284: the 973,312 km2 shape is far above the infobox's 100,000 km2 at 1250; the early shape is cut to the Sosso lands and then, from 1241, to the full Cliopatria outline without Takrur and the Niger bend. The infobox figure and the Sundiata and Mali pages' text disagree; the expansion dates are undated on both pages, so the 1241 gains are bridges (confidence 1) and a gap-filler should find a source that dates Sundiata's and Sakura's conquests. (2) Takrur is taken out until c. 1285 on the Takrur page's date; the Mali page says Sundiata's generals reached it. (3) Timbuktu and Gao are taken out until c. 1300/1324, and Timbuktu, Gao and Oualata are taken out again from 1433-1436; Cliopatria keeps them until 1468. (4) The 1564 shape holds from 1537 and the last shape ends 1610. Not settled: the 1415 growth (+141,000 km2) and the 1463/1468/1475 drops are not explained by the pages beyond Mema 1465 and Songhai's wars; the 1475 loss is a confidence-1 bridge. Mansa Uli, Wati, Khalifa, Abu Bakr, Sakura (coup 1285), Maghan I (c. 1337, deposed 1341), Suleyman (death 1360), Mari Djata II, Musa II (died 1387) have no territorial events on the pages; no ruler strip because the pages do not give a complete list with years. Counterparts needing dossiers: kaabu (independent 1537), jolof-empire (c. 1360), the Tuareg of Timbuktu/Takedda, and the pre-imperial Gao kingdom (here mapped to songhai-empire). The Seshat page for Mali (ml_mali_emp) failed to load twice. The Jolof vassal pair (1241-1360) and the Wuli vassal pair (1576-1610) are paired in the ledger with identical counterpart strings. Gazetteer names used: none missing (Oualata, Kangaba, Koulikoro, Nioro du Sahel, Gao, Timbuktu resolve; Mema, Kita and Diafunu have no entry, so Kayes and Nioro du Sahel are proxies).
